short_description: Browse Notion and tick tasks off from the BUSY Bar
description:
Your Notion pages and to-dos on the BUSY Bar: your top-level pages and databases, then whatever a page holds, its subpages, databases, toggles, headings and to-dos, in the page's own order.

A database shows its open tasks due today, overdue or undated, and the ones ticked off today; the Show setting switches to all open tasks. Up to 20 rows. In a database with a status, you choose the status right on the bar. A change made in Notion shows on the bar within seconds.

- **Wheel**: moves through the list.
- **OK** or **Start**: opens a page or a toggle, or ticks a task off with a burst of confetti; OK again unticks it.
- **Back**: goes up a level; on the top level, leaves the app.

The bar talks to the Notion API itself over Wi-Fi: no computer, server or proxy. Your token and your pages go only between the bar and api.notion.com, under [Notion's Privacy Policy](https://www.notion.com/trust/privacy-policy).

## First start

1. Open [app.notion.com/developers/tokens](https://app.notion.com/developers/tokens), create a new personal access token with access to the Notion API and copy it ([Notion's guide](https://developers.notion.com/guides/connections-and-tokens/personal-access-tokens)).
2. Start the app on the bar. The back display shows the address of the bar's web interface: http://10.0.4.20 over USB, or the bar's address on Wi-Fi.
3. Open that address in a browser, go to **Apps**, then **Tasks for Notion**, and paste the token into **Notion token**.
4. Your top-level pages appear on the bar in a few seconds.

On some Notion plans only workspace owners can create a personal access token. An internal connection works too, and sees only the pages you share with it: create it in Notion's developer portal with Read content and Update content, paste its token the same way, then add the connection to the pages you want on the bar.
